source_documents.title: A novel ratiometric fluorescent probe through aggregation-induced emission and analyte-induced excimer dissociation

conditions_studied: DMSO, DMF, EA, DCM, MeOH, n-hexane, MeCN, THF

reference_evidence_units.quote: The disappearance of fluorescence is caused by the ICT effect in which intramolecular charge transfer occurs from the electron-donating anthracene moiety to the electron-accepting aldehyde group.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9-anthraldehyde
reference_evidence_units.statement: Non-emission in solution assigned to anthracene→aldehyde ICT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Asserted: non-emissive in all solvents including n-hexane; no solvatochromism or calculation shown.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a new and strong emission peak emerges at 516 nm (Fig. 2a), which corresponds to the excimer emission of the fluorophore.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9-anthraldehyde
reference_evidence_units.statement: 516 nm excimer band appears with water (90-fold at 99%).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Because water is a poor solvent for 9-anthraldehyde, the fluorophore molecules must have aggregated in the solution with high water contents, and the aggregation leads to the excimer emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: 9-anthraldehyde
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregates (80-100 nm by TEM) give excimer emission.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper's explanation of the dark solution state. Weak: the only basis is non-emission in all good solvents (including n-hexane); no solvatochromism, rate or calculation.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Aggregation in water produces the 516 nm excimer emission; sulfite adduct formation dissociates it.
